paras: The Newmarket hotel whipping was the flogging of two young Black men by a crowd of white men at Newmarket (also printed New Market), Alabama, in early September 1903, after the men walked into the dining room of the town's hotel and ordered supper. Each man was given fifty lashes, and one account says they were then run out of town. The item ran in at least five white newspapers within four days, and a Montgomery editor presented it as a lesson connected to a recent dining-room controversy at Hamlet, North Carolina.

The hotel at Newmarket was run by Mrs. Hambrick, whom the Alexandria Gazette described as "a white woman." None of the reports names the two men; the Huntsville correspondent called them "two young negro men," while the Gazette called them "two strange negroes."

On a Thursday night, by the Gazette's account, the two men entered the hotel dining room and ordered supper. According to the Huntsville special printed in Birmingham and Montgomery, they were told to get out, and their reply to the proprietress was "insolent." The Gazette gave a different reason for the alarm, saying the men "it is thought, believed she was alone," and that Mrs. Hambrick notified a male relative who happened to be in the house.

The relative knocked the two men down and kicked them out of the house. A crowd of white men then took them in hand and gave each fifty lashes, with a rawhide whip according to the Huntsville special. The Gazette added that the crowd tied the men to trees, whipped them publicly on their naked backs, and then ran them out of the town.
No report names the relative or anyone in the crowd, and no report of arrests, charges or any official inquiry appears in the coverage.

The Huntsville correspondent's dispatch, dated September 4, appeared the next day in the Birmingham Age-Herald under the headline "NEGROES RECEIVE SOUND THRASHING" and in the Montgomery Advertiser as "NEGROES ARE BEATEN." The Age-Herald's subhead presented the whipping as punishment, saying the men were "THROWN OUT AND WHIPPED FOR THEIR INSOLENCE," and its text said they had "took it into their heads" to enjoy a meal at the hotel. The same text, re-dated Newmarket, September 5, ran in the San Antonio Daily Light on September 6 as "NEGROES RAWHIDED," subtitled "They Went Into a Restaurant and Got Insulting When Ordered Out."

The Alexandria Gazette carried its own, more detailed version on September 5 as one item in its "News of the Day" digest, without comment. On September 8 the Raleigh News & Observer reprinted a comment from the Montgomery Journal under the headline "BAD EXAMPLE GOES FAR," subtitled "Wanted to Do Like Bocker [Booker] and Party and Got Fifty Lashes." The Journal said its Huntsville special, "anent the negro dining room incident at Hamlet, N. C.," was "not without significance" and "points a moral and adorns a tale."

Every version came from the white press and gave the white side's account, stating the men's "insolence" as fact and quoting neither of them. No account of the whipping in the Black press appears in the coverage.

The Gazette placed the whipping on Thursday night, September 3, while the San Antonio Daily Light, under a September 5 dateline, said it happened "yesterday," September 4. Because the Daily Light's text otherwise follows the Huntsville dispatch of September 4 almost word for word, its later date appears to be a re-dating rather than independent information. The accounts also differ on why the men were attacked: the Huntsville special cited their "insolent" reply when ordered out, while the Gazette mentioned no exchange and said only that they were thought to believe the proprietress was alone.

reader.title: Newmarket hotel whipping
bases: A crowd of white men seized two Black men who had ordered supper in a hotel dining room and gave each fifty lashes (A1, A2); no organized band, warning or campaign is reported, so the whitecapping label is not supported.

The Huntsville special (A2, A3, A4, A5) and the separately worded Alexandria Gazette item, which adds details absent from it (A1), agree on the core event: two Black men ordered supper at Mrs. Hambrick's hotel, were knocked down and put out, and were given fifty lashes each by a crowd of white men.
